At Google, almost 16% of tests show some flakiness.

lines.text: And every team rebuilds the same plumbing: waits, drivers, screenshots and reports, once for web, again for mobile, and again for API.
SHAFT is one open-source Java engine for web, mobile, API, database and command-line tests.
It is built on the standards your team already trusts: Selenium, Appium and REST Assured.
Waiting is built in, so your tests stop guessing when a page is ready.
Every run produces an Allure report with steps and screenshots that anyone on the team can read.
And the same tests move from a laptop to a Selenium Grid or BrowserStack by changing one setting.
Adopting it is low risk. The upgrade tool compiles your project first, keeps your existing tests, and restores every file if anything fails.
AI help is optional. Capture, Doctor and Heal work without any AI provider.
SHAFT is MIT licensed and built in public since 2018, with 216 releases from 62 contributors.
